title: ADG common contract definitions (v1)
description: Shared definitions referenced by every ADG collector contract. Collectors report observations; they never report conclusions. See docs/contracts/collector-protocol.md.

schemaVersion.title: Contract schema version
schemaVersion.description: Major version 1. A minor bump is additive and backward compatible; a breaking change requires a new major directory (v2) and a migration note.

sid.title: Security identifier
sid.description: String-form SID. The canonical identity of every principal: upper-case S, no leading zeros, decimal identifier authority below 2^32 and 0x-prefixed hexadecimal above. Names are never identity.

domainSid.title: Domain or machine SID
domainSid.description: A SID of the form S-1-5-21-x-y-z with no RID.

timestamp.title: Timezone-aware timestamp
timestamp.description: RFC 3339 timestamp that MUST carry an offset (Z or +/-HH:MM). A naive timestamp is rejected: observations from hosts in different time zones would otherwise be unorderable.

sourceKey.title: Stable source key
sourceKey.description: Deterministic identity of the observed object, derived only from its identifying fields. Ingestion is idempotent on (run_id, source_key). The derivation for each observation kind is fixed in docs/contracts/collector-protocol.md and is recomputed and verified server-side.

accessMask.title: Windows access mask
accessMask.description: Raw unsigned 32-bit access mask exactly as read from the descriptor, generic bits included. Collectors must not expand generic rights or otherwise interpret the mask.

aceFlags.title: Raw ACE header flags
aceFlags.description: The ACE_HEADER.AceFlags byte: OBJECT_INHERIT 0x01, CONTAINER_INHERIT 0x02, NO_PROPAGATE_INHERIT 0x04, INHERIT_ONLY 0x08, INHERITED 0x10. Unknown bits are preserved rather than dropped.

aclHash.title: Normalized DACL digest
aclHash.description: SHA-256, lower-case hexadecimal, taken over the canonical normalized form of the DACL (docs/architecture/ntfs-acl-normalization.md). It covers dacl_present, dacl_protected, and the ACEs' trustee/type/mask/flags in evaluation order; it deliberately excludes the owner, because every folder under a root is legitimately owned by whoever created it while sharing one inherited DACL. Added in contract 1.2.

resourceKind.title: What kind of file-system object a resource observation describes
resourceKind.description: Directories are the default and the only kind contract 1.2 could express. File-level scanning is opt-in in a collector and reports 'file'; a file is never traversed, and it inherits through the object projection (OBJECT_INHERIT) rather than the container one. Added in contract 1.3.

aclBoundaryReason.title: Why a resource is reported as a place where permissions change
aclBoundaryReason.description: Non-null exactly when is_acl_boundary is true. A bare boolean cannot tell 'an administrator set permissions here' from 'the collector could not see the parent, so it does not know' - two findings that call for different responses. The four unknowable reasons (share_root, scan_root, parent_unreadable, parent_null_dacl) all report is_acl_boundary true: a boundary that is not there costs one extra stored ACL, while a boundary reported false tells a later scan it may stop looking. Added in contract 1.3.

aceType.description: DACL entry type. Audit (SACL) entries govern logging, not access, and must never be reported here.

aceSource.description: Whether the ACE was set on this object or inherited from an ancestor. Must agree with bit 0x10 of ace_flags.

groupType.description: Distribution groups never grant access. 'unknown' means the source did not say, which must not be reported as 'harmless'.

membershipEdgeKind.description: primary_group exists because primaryGroupID membership does not appear in a group's member attribute; omitting it under-reports access for every user in the domain.

sharePermission.description: The three levels reported by the SMB management cmdlets.

hostName.title: Windows host name
hostName.description: A host name alone, never a UNC path and never a path fragment.

uncPath.title: Canonical UNC path
uncPath.description: Absolute UNC path identifying a resource: \\server\share[\path]. Relative paths, '.' and '..' segments, drive-letter paths, and extended-length prefixes are rejected; a resource identified only by a local path is ambiguous because the server is unknown.

localPath.title: Drive-letter path on the server
localPath.description: Supplementary only. A local path never identifies a resource on its own.

scopeKind.title: Reconciliation scope kind
scopeKind.description: What a run claims to have enumerated completely. Absence of an object may only be inferred inside a scope a successful run reconciled.

key.description: Identity of the scope: a domain SID, a case-folded host name, a share key, or a canonical UNC path.

source.title: Observation source
source.description: Who saw the fact and how. The reading method is evidence, not a label: different mechanisms report different detail (share permissions as levels versus masks, for instance).

collectionMode.title: Collection mode (contract 1.4)
collectionMode.description: Why a run is or is not incremental. 'full' read every object in its scopes; 'delta' read only what the source reported as changed since a checkpoint and may never reconcile; 'reconcile' is a full read whose purpose is to repair what the deltas could not see. `incremental` MUST be true if and only if the mode is 'delta'.

checkpointKind.title: Checkpoint cursor kind (contract 1.4)
checkpointKind.description: How a checkpoint's token may be compared. 'usn' is a monotonic per-server counter (uSNChanged) and is ordered only against the same issuer; 'timestamp' is a replicated change time, ordered only to the second and only as well as the clocks involved; 'opaque' is a collector-private cursor the server stores and never interprets.

collectorCheckpoint.title: Collector checkpoint (contract 1.4)
collectorCheckpoint.description: How far a delta run got, and who issued the cursor. The issuer is required and is compared: a uSNChanged watermark is a counter local to one domain controller, so DC1's number replayed against DC2 would silently skip every object whose USN on DC2 falls below it, and a DC restored from backup reissues numbers it has already handed out. The server refuses a checkpoint it cannot show to be ahead of the stored one, and records the refusal.

token.description: The cursor. A decimal integer for 'usn', an RFC 3339 timestamp with an offset for 'timestamp', anything the collector likes for 'opaque'.

issuer.description: Whatever the cursor is local to. For a domain controller, its dsServiceName and invocationId joined: the first changes when the collector binds a different DC, the second when the same DC is restored from backup.

affirmation.title: Affirmation (contract 1.4)
affirmation.description: An object this scan re-read and found unchanged, sent as a key and a digest instead of the whole object. It exists because the file system has no change metadata a DACL edit reliably touches - writing an ACL does not move LastWriteTime - so a scan that skipped unchanged directories on a timestamp would skip exactly the changes ADG is for. The collector therefore still reads every descriptor; what it sends for the unchanged ones is this. The digest MUST be computed from this scan's reading and never copied from the collector's record of what it sent last time. The server compares it against the digest it holds and REFUSES the affirmation when they differ, naming it in the response so the collector re-sends the object in full. An affirmed object counts as observed: it extends the object's timeline, and a run that affirmed everything it did not re-send has still enumerated its whole scope and may reconcile it.

kind.description: Only 'ntfs_resource' may be affirmed in contract 1.4. It is the one kind with a published whole-object digest (acl_hash, contract 1.2) that the server already recomputes from what it stores.

digest.description: The kind's content digest as this scan read it. For 'ntfs_resource' it is exactly the acl_hash of contract 1.2 - over the whole DACL, in the reading being affirmed, including dacl_present and dacl_protected.
